kind: synthetic: every number below comes from the logistic map and the assumptions in scenarios.json; nothing is measured in the Demerzel repository
rounding: exponents to 6 decimals, step counts and digits to 2 decimals, shares and ratios to 4 decimals, states to 6 decimals, gaps and required errors to 3 significant digits; a mean of step counts is rounded half up from the integer total stored next to it
arithmetic: IEEE 754 doubles with +, -, * and / only, plus one correctly rounded square root; ln and exp are series built from those operations; random.Random(seed).random() supplies the starting points; the section high_precision repeats some runs on Python integers

map.name: logistic map
map.note: A textbook model chosen because every quantity in the lesson can be computed for it. It is not a model of the project.

starting_points.draw: 0.1 + 0.8 * random.Random(seed).random(), one draw per starting point, the same draws for every regime

perturbation_rule: the second run starts at x + error when x < 0.5 and at x - error otherwise, so that it stays inside the interval

chaotic_r4.expected_attractor: chaotic, the whole interval from 0 to 1

lyapunov_settings.cited_comparison_source: MAT-024, Dynamical Systems, Stability and Feedback, section 2, table of exponents (Demerzel commit 4b03838800dcd4894f1e026461979bff1d985ca8, state/streeling/courses/mathematics/en/mat-024-dynamical-systems-stability-feedback.md)

gap_table.definition: Each starting point is run twice, the second run initial_error away; the gap is the absolute difference between the two runs at the same step. Gaps are rounded to 3 significant digits.

exponent_from_median_gaps.formula: exponent = ln(later_gap / earlier_gap) / (to_step - from_step), from the rounded median gaps above; the last field of each estimate averages ln(gap ratio) over the pairs instead, from the unrounded gaps
exponent_from_median_gaps.rule: from step 0 to the last tabulated step at which the median gap is still usable: below small_gap_limit (growth not yet slowed by the size of the attractor) and at least floor_in_spacings spacings of doubles (not yet lost in rounding)

horizon.definition: Horizon of a pair = the first step at which its two runs differ by at least the tolerance. formula_steps = ln(tolerance / initial_error) / exponent. mean_minus_formula and steps_per_digit are computed from the rounded figures of this table, so that they can be checked by hand.

wanted_horizon.formula: required initial error = tolerance * e^(-exponent * steps)

known_value.reason: At r = 4 the substitution x = sin^2(pi * t) turns the map into t -> 2t mod 1, for which the uniform distribution of t is invariant; x < 0.25 holds for t in [0, 1/6) and (5/6, 1], a set of length 1/3.

high_precision.arithmetic: Python integers: a state is a whole number of 2^-1024 (about 308 decimal digits); one step is r * x * (1 - x) with exact products and one truncation, for the exact value of the double r and from the same starting doubles as the other sections

error_bound.formula: (4^steps - 1) / 3 * 2^-bits: one step multiplies an earlier error by at most 4 and truncates by less than 2^-bits

beyond_the_horizon.starts: the same two doubles as in beyond_the_horizon, converted exactly

exercise_4.formula: required initial error = tolerance * e^(-exponent * steps)

option_b.definition: A pair stays within tolerance through an interval of k steps when its horizon (first step at or above the tolerance) is later than k. A forecast stays within tolerance through the wanted span when the gap is below the tolerance at every step of it, the forecast run restarting from the true state with a fresh initial error every k steps.

phase_error_in_the_two_cycle.note: In the two-cycle regime, start the second run on the other point of the cycle: an error too large to count as small.

transfer_task.note: Hypothetical delivery simulator for the learner task. Not Streeling data and not a forecast.

calm.reading: the error shrinks, so no horizon limits the forecast
